findings.title: A QR image read as secret input leaves its file bytes and decoded pixels unwiped
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Low: needs access to the process memory; the decoded text itself cannot be wiped in JavaScript.
findings.reproduction: docs/audits/AUD-018-harnesses/probes.ts, first case: the public record MNC1:direct:indexes with eleven 1s and a 4 (abandon … about) is saved with exportQrPayload and read with decodeQrPngFile; the bytes that readFileOrRefuse hands over and the RGBA data that pngjs decodes are captured.
findings.expected: bounded-read.ts: "the one copy returned is the caller's to wipe"; SECURITY.md: temporary copies of the phrase data are cleared as far as possible. The text reader does so (input.ts decodedText), as the probe's control shows.
findings.observed: After a successful read both buffers still hold their content: fileWiped false, pixelsWiped false. The control (readBoundedTextFile) wipes its bytes.
findings.impact: An encoded record or a share given as a QR image stays in the heap as PNG bytes (up to 16 MiB) and as decoded pixels (about 2 MB for a 720-pixel code) until the memory is reused. Core dumps are off and the permission model applies, so reading it needs access to the process memory, swap or a hibernation image. jsQR's own working copies and the decoded string cannot be wiped.
findings.recommendedFix: In decodeQrPngFile, wipe the file bytes and image.data in a finally block, on success and refusal alike, as decodedText does for text; add the probe as a regression test.
findings.requiredVerification: The probe's first case passes; the QR tests and the CLI self-test still pass.

findings.title: README card and QR examples combine --ask-secrets with --dates, which the CLI refuses
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Low: the edit is not committed; the committed README has no such example.
affectedFiles: README.md (uncommitted edit), section Cards and QR codes, lines 321-331
findings.reproduction: node dist/mnemocode.js encode --mode seedshift --ask-secrets --dates 23-09-2026 --format 5 --cards < /dev/null; the same with --qr my-palette-qr.png. The decode --qr-file my-palette-qr.png example after them needs that file.
findings.expected: Every README example runs as written; the README's own table says that --ask-secrets asks for the dates on the private screen.
findings.observed: Both refused before any prompt: "mnemocode: --ask-secrets cannot be combined with --dates.", exit 1. The committed README (HEAD) has no example that combines them: the uncommitted edit added them.
findings.impact: A person who follows the examples gets an error and may move the phrase to --mnemonic, where the shell history keeps it. No secret is exposed by the tool itself.
findings.evidence: AUD-018-evidence/readme-examples.log (local); direct run recorded in this report
findings.recommendedFix: Drop --dates 23-09-2026 from the two encode examples (the dates are asked on the private screen), or show the public --mnemonic form for a demonstration.
findings.requiredVerification: readme-examples.py: the corrected commands pass, or are skipped only for their secret prompt; a manual run with the prompts confirms the QR round trip.

findings.title: Audit records cite commits that the current history no longer holds
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Low: findings and outcomes are unaffected; only the published snapshot references cannot be followed.
findings.reproduction: python3 docs/audits/AUD-018-harnesses/record-integrity.py; git merge-base --is-ancestor <commit> HEAD for each cited commit.
findings.expected: AGENTS.md: a commit that an audit record names is changed only together with that record, whose hashes are then updated. CHECK-DOC-003: cross-report references resolve.
findings.observed: 14 citations of four commits do not resolve. b4f334f… and 5547c9e… (MnemoCode) are reachable only from local backup refs, not from main or origin; their counterparts with the same subject are 6d9100e… and 2705bf1…. f17c323… has no counterpart with the same subject. c76141f… is not an ancestor of multi-chain-wallet-tools HEAD.
findings.impact: A reader cannot check the AUD-001 and AUD-002 reviewed and fixed snapshots on GitHub, nor AUD-010's schema reference.
findings.recommendedFix: With the owner's decision: cite the current counterparts (6d9100e29922ae3bcc964989fdedc93710ff56ef and 2705bf15558bd760daadf189fbf0ed727446eae7), say for f17c323… that the reviewed snapshot is not published, and cite multi-chain's current commit of the schema in AUD-010.

publishNewFolder checks the target with absentPath and then renames the staging folder; POSIX rename replaces an empty folder that another local process creates in between. Only an empty folder can be replaced; not reported as a finding.
Rendered PDFs and written QR images are not wiped after they are saved: pdf-lib and qrcode keep their own copies, and the documents describe wiping only for the byte arrays a part owns.

Harness mistake, kept in the evidence: the first run-checks.sh put --timeout before the label, so two checks did not start (an empty local --timeout.log and a refused label). Corrected and run under their own labels; no result was lost.

limitations: Single reviewer (Claude Code, no subagents, no independent skeptic) at the owner's request.
Not run: the 11 PDF-rendering test files, card goldens, check-card-output.mjs, the Docker rebuild of the SSKR engine, the executable build, Windows and macOS, CI, and any release step.
The README examples that ask for secrets or draw PDFs were not run.

The source review was risk-based: input and file boundaries, process protection, randomness and encryption, the candidate-file change, the newest remediation code, documents and records; not every line of the 43,000 lines of source was read.
The snapshot includes another agent's uncommitted README edit and the uncommitted candidate-file admission change.

remediationAddendum.statusRule: Fixed, not verified: no commit holds the fixes yet.

fixes.change: decodeQrPngFile loads its decoders first, then reads, decodes and wipes in one step: the file bytes and the decoded pixels are wiped through the shared wipedAfter rule, after a code is read and when the image is refused. test/aud-018.test.ts holds the probe's case and three more: an image without a code, a file that is no PNG, and the text reader's control.

The two encode examples no longer give --dates with --ask-secrets; the dates are asked on the private screen. readme-secret-arguments.py runs every README example with --ask-secrets up to its terminal check.

The index already said that the AUD-001 and AUD-002 identifiers cannot be opened on main; it now names their counterparts in the current history (6d9100e29922ae3bcc964989fdedc93710ff56ef and 2705bf15558bd760daadf189fbf0ed727446eae7, same message and source fingerprint) and says that f17c323… has no commit of its own. The AUD-001 and AUD-002 records stay as they were. AUD-010 cites multi-chain-wallet-tools c82bcace05eed8840610312a498b05528965baa7, its current commit of the schema file with the same bytes (d47df012…). record-integrity.py now accepts a citation that the index explains or that the multi-chain checkout holds.
